newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed amid uncertain prospects.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed amid uncertain prospects.

text.p: Argentine bonds ended mixed Friday in thin trading with political worries re-emerging to knock local bonds lower.

Although the market's worries over political corruption accusations subsided in the last two sessions, an analyst said the "market is cautious because one does not know when the issues will re-emerge."
"If corruption starts to be discovered at high levels, one does not know at what levels it will stop," he added.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.15 to 118.45.
Traders said the decline in U.S. treasuries off their early highs added to the downward pressure on Argentine bonds in the afternoon.

However, Argentine Brady debt managed to remain in positive territory, as traders said the uncertainty around the corruption talk appeared to be having a larger impact on local than foreign investors.
A trader at a large Argentine brokerage house said "market expectations are not very good - next week is going to be a difficult week."
And the analyst said "for the moment it is best to cautious and not take out new positions."

All the same analysts and traders agree that if one looks strictly at Argentina's economic situation then bonds should be supported. Economic activity is bouncing back and economists predict the economy will pick up more steam in the coming year.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 7.60 percent from 7.50 percent.
